html_body:
🎯 Stock Finder — Momentum Shortlist

Tuesday, September 1, 2026 — Kuwait time

Thin day — 3 candidates cleared the gates

~25 tickers surfaced across 20+ web searches and IBKR topic discovery. Most bullish narratives didn't hold up against live IBKR data — one (RBRK) looked like the best setup in the batch until its own price history showed a -13% reversal the very next session. Best setup today: ESTC.

How this was screened

Every candidate below was checked against IBKR daily price history (not just a snapshot) before being shortlisted — several search-reported "movers" turned out to be flat or fading once the actual bars were pulled. Stop/target levels are derived from real recent highs/lows/gap-day ranges shown for each name, not percentage guesses.

⚠️ Cap-size balance note

No small-cap name cleared the gates today. The one small-cap candidate with a real technical footprint (SOPH) turned out to be stale — 2 weeks of sideways chop near its highs, not a fresh move — and thin on liquidity besides. Today's 3 survivors are 2 large-cap + 1 mid-cap.

Momentum Shortlist

Run analyze [TICKER] on any name for the full deep dive before entering.
#1 — ESTC | Elastic N.V. 3/5 ⭐⭐⭐ $97.55 MID CAP

Data analytics / search software

Signal: Gapped from $83.74 close to a $103.89 open on Aug 28 (Q2 beat + raised guidance, +24% gap on 7.1M shares vs ~1M average) — 2 trading days ago. Aug 29-31 consolidated in a $95.36-$102.42 range, holding well above the gap-day low.

Price: $97.55 (IBKR) | Avg daily $ vol: ~$218M (excellent liquidity) | vs 52w range: 9.6% below the $107.89 post-earnings/52-week high, +132% off the $42.07 52-week low.

Why it's interesting: Clean post-earnings structure — the gap held, the stock hasn't given the move back, and it's still holding a fresh higher-low above the breakout-day range. Best risk/reward of the three survivors.

Realistic near-term target: +6-11% over 3-7 trading days — retest of the $103.50 post-gap intraday zone, then the $108 breakout high.

Entry read: BUY AT MARKET / limit near current — not extended, sitting mid-range of its post-earnings consolidation.

Order plan (GTC, all legs together):
BUY limit $97.75 · stop-limit trigger $95.00 / limit $94.50 (below the Aug 31 post-earnings low of $95.36) · TP1 sell limit $103.50 · TP2 $108.00 (breakout-day high) · size ~0.82 shares ≈ $80 (~15% of $535.68 net liq) · R:R ≈ 1.8:1 to TP1, ≈ 3.2:1 to TP2
Event window: earnings behind it ✅ Halal: ✅ Verified — search/data analytics software

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear  |  Next step: analyze ESTC
#2 — OKTA | Okta Inc. 2/5 ⭐⭐ $173.20 LARGE CAP

Identity / cybersecurity SaaS

Signal: Gapped from a $134.42 close to a $166.15 open on Aug 27 (Q2 beat + raised guidance, +23.5% gap on 11.0M shares vs ~1.3M average) — 3 trading days ago. Held the gap, made a new high of $174.85 on Aug 31.

Price: $173.20 (IBKR, live) | Avg daily $ vol: ~$590M (exceptional liquidity) | vs 52w range: sitting at 99% of its $174.85 52-week high, +176% off the 52-week low.

Why it's interesting: Real, confirmed, high-volume breakout with textbook liquidity. The catch: it's sitting right at a fresh 52-week high with no overhead resistance to measure a target against, and the only clean invalidation level (the $156.50 gap-day low) is ~10% away — a poor risk/reward to chase here.

Realistic near-term target: +5-9% over 3-7 trading days if it holds the recent higher-low structure.

Entry read: WAIT FOR PULLBACK to $165-168 (the Aug 28/31 close zone) — do not chase at $173. Correct thesis, but current entry gives a bad R:R.

Order plan (GTC, all legs together):
BUY limit $167.50 (resting — only fills on the pullback) · stop-limit trigger $163.80 / limit $163.20 (below the Aug 31 low of $164.50) · TP1 sell limit $182.00 · size ~0.48 shares ≈ $80 (~15% of $535.68 net liq) · R:R ≈ 3.4:1
Event window: earnings behind it ✅ Halal: ✅ Verified — identity/access management software

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear  |  Next step: analyze OKTA
#3 — DG | Dollar General Corp. 1/5 ⭐ $126.75 LARGE CAP

Discount retail

Signal: Q2 beat + raised full-year EPS guidance ($7.80-8.00 vs prior $7.20-7.45) drove a gap to a $132.50 high on Aug 27 (3.8M shares vs ~1.6-2M average) — 4 trading days ago. Pulled back to $121.34 on Aug 28, then bounced to close $126.75 on Aug 31.

Price: $126.75 (IBKR) | Avg daily $ vol: ~$338M (excellent liquidity) | vs 52w range: 19.4% below the $157.31 52-week high, well above the $94.49 52-week low.

Why it's interesting: Fresh guidance-raise catalyst with a real pullback-and-hold pattern. Weakest of the three on conviction score — it's already given back part of the pop and the stop has to sit fairly far below to stay valid, so the R:R to TP1 is thin. Included for cap-size balance, not as a high-conviction pick.

Realistic near-term target: +4-7% over 5-8 trading days — retest of the $132.50 breakout high, stretch to $136.

Entry read: BUY AT MARKET / limit near current — already pulled back once, not chasing the initial gap.

Order plan (GTC, all legs together):
BUY limit $127.00 · stop-limit trigger $121.00 / limit $120.50 (below the Aug 28 pullback low of $121.34) · TP1 sell limit $132.50 · TP2 $136.00 · size ~0.63 shares ≈ $80 (~15% of $535.68 net liq) · R:R ≈ 0.85:1 to TP1, ≈ 1.4:1 to TP2

⚠️ Sizing note: R:R to TP1 is below 1:1 — this only works if it can run to TP2. On an ~$80 position, the ~$2 round-trip commission is ~2.5% of the position, so this needs a clean move to clear costs plus a real gain.

Event window: earnings behind it ✅ Halal: ✅ Verified — discount general merchandise retail

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear  |  Next step: analyze DG

🏆 Today's best setup

ESTC (Elastic) — the cleanest post-earnings structure of the batch: the Aug 28 guidance-raise gap has held for 3 sessions without giving the move back, liquidity is excellent, and the stop sits close enough below the recent low to give a genuinely good risk/reward (better than OKTA's, which is more extended, and better than DG's, which already gave back part of its pop). Invalidation: a close back below $95.36 (the Aug 31 post-earnings low) — that says the gap failed to hold and the thesis is wrong.

Cut this run — showing the work

RBRK (Rubrik) — FADED, hard. Search found a fresh Citi Buy/PT-$130 note, and IBKR showed it hit a new 52-week high ($107.91) on Aug 27 — but the very next session it reversed -13% on 6.5M shares and closed near a fresh 2-week low. The bullish analyst note almost certainly predates that reversal. Textbook case of trusting IBKR over the narrative.
BIDU — search said shares were "rising significantly" on an HK dual-listing catalyst; IBKR shows it 42% below its 52-week high and sitting right at its 52-week low. Faded/stale.
CPRI (Capri Holdings) — JPMorgan upgrade with a $30 target, but the stock is trading at $13.25, essentially at its 52-week low. An analyst's hope, not live price action.
CHA (Chagee) — Macquarie upgrade; stock is 39% below its 52-week high with no confirming move. No live signal.
MGA (Magna) — analyst PT raise; stock is sitting right at its 13-week low. No momentum confirmed.
CCJ (Cameco, NYSE) — recovering off a 13-week low but still 27% below its 52-week high; the PT raise cited was on the Toronto-listed shares. Not fresh enough.
GAP (Gap Inc.) — reported pop from a week+ ago; live quote showed flat (0.0% change) and 23% off the 52-week high. Unconfirmed.
SOPH (SOPHiA Genetics) — real name, but 2 weeks of sideways chop in an $8.03-$8.98 range — no move in the last 5 sessions, and thin ($3.4M avg daily $ volume). Stale.
NEOG (Neogen) — Piper Sandler PT raise; price has drifted flat in an $11.43-$12.26 range for 2 weeks. No signal.
COHR (Coherent Corp) — "surging" on a conference presentation per search; IBKR shows it still 37% below its 13-week/52-week high of $440. No breakout.
ALAB (Astera Labs) — AI-infra theme name via IBKR's semiconductor theme list; choppy $266-$310 range for 2 weeks, 40% off its highs, no fresh catalyst this week.
CCEC (Capital Clean Energy Carriers) — plausible LNG-shipping earnings-beat story, but IBKR returned no market data at all for this contract. Can't confirm, can't include.
SBSW (Sibanye-Stillwater) — "premarket gainer" story tied to today's earnings; live snapshot showed 0.0% change and historical range data timed out. Insufficient confirmation.
NVDA and other mega-cap AI names — already all over mainstream financial media this week; skipped per the skill's own "don't cover the obvious" rule.
SEZL, CHYM, ENVA (Sezzle, Chime, Enova) — strong momentum stories, but core business is consumer lending/neobanking (BNPL, online installment credit, digital banking) — excluded on the halal business-activity screen (interest-based finance as the primary business).
TD (Toronto-Dominion Bank) — conventional bank. Excluded, halal.
XLY (Auxly Cannabis) — cannabis. Excluded, halal.
